Claire — thanks, this is helpful. Attached is a one-page trade study plus a small workbook (aegisbio_kv_quant_workbook.xlsx) with model-by-model memory curves. High level notes here so the team has something to react to quickly: 

Summary (TL;DR)
- KV-cache footprint increases roughly linearly with context length and is the dominant incremental GPU memory consumer for long contexts. Expect ~0.45 GB of KV per 1k tokens for the 70B baseline when using our optimized KV layout (float16 activations).
- Quantization (weight-only int8) reduces model parameter memory by ~45% vs fp16, but does not reduce KV cache size significantly. Activation-aware or ldq-style quant (mixed-int8/activation) can cut peak activation working set by another ~10-15% in realistic decoding paths.
- For pilot: with 10 concurrent sessions averaging 12k context and burst to 24k, recommend reserving 4 x A100-40GB-equivalent GPUs (on Redwood Dedicated) with aggressive prefix caching and a small per-request KV eligibility policy.
- For production (50 concurrent, average 18k context): recommend 18 x A100-40GB-equivalent (or 10 x A100-80GB / 16 x QL-100 if using bigger memory cards or more aggressive quant).

Key quantitative points (workbook has full matrices)
- Model param memory (fp16) for 70B: ~35 GB. Weight-only int8 brings that to ~19.5 GB (45% reduction).
- KV-cache: at 2 bytes/element (fp16 activations compressed), estimate 0.45 GB per 1k tokens. So a 24k context implies ~10.8 GB KV. Add ~10 GB params (if int8 weights with some fp16 activations) = ~20.8 GB peak working set per active session.
- If using fp16 end-to-end: 35 GB params + 10.8 GB KV = ~45.8 GB peak => requires >1x 40GB card, so you'd need multi-GPU sharding or larger instances.
- With weight-only int8 + activation-aware quant: 19.5 GB params + 9.2 GB KV (slightly lower due to compression) + ~3 GB for decoder activations/overhead = ~31.7 GB per session. That fits comfortably on a single 40GB card for one session, but concurrency must be handled by pooling/batching.

Sizing examples (with our runtime assumptions: asynchronous batching, KV reuse, 4ms per-token kernel latency on the chosen ops)
- Pilot (10 concurrent, 12k avg, bursts to 24k):
  - Option A (fp16 baseline): need roughly 12 x 40GB cards (sharded sessions) or 6 x 80GB to keep p95 < 600ms with low batching.
  - Option B (weight-only int8 + activation-aware): 4 x 40GB-equivalent GPUs with aggressive request routing and prefix cache covering templates and commonly-seen chunks (saves ~25% of KV reads).
- Production (50 concurrent, 18k avg):
  - Option A (fp16): ~24 x 40GB-equivalent GPUs or 12 x 80GB to meet latency SLOs under the expected QPS distribution.
  - Option B (int8 + runtime optimizations + KV offload to host NVMe for cold prefixes): ~18 x 40GB-equivalent or 10 x 80GB with some KV offload and extra headroom.

Operational notes / tradeoffs
- KV-cache is the easy win for cost reduction: prefix caching + cold KV offload can reduce active GPU memory by 20-40% depending on prompt reuse. If AegisBio patterns are templated (many common sections), caching will pay for itself quickly.
- Int8 weight-only quantization is a high-leverage win for parameter-heavy models; it reduces cost but watch for a small uptick in decoding latency depending on kernel support. Activation-aware quant helps further but increases complexity in onboarding and verification.
- We recommend a staged approach: pilot with weight-only int8 + prefix caching, validate quality/regression on your eval suite, then enable activation-aware quant and KV offload for production roll.

Next steps I propose:
1) Dylan & Lauren: validate the workbook assumptions with AegisBio example traces (Tom, can you drop a week of anonymized trace with token-level lengths?)
2) I'll produce a proposed reserved capacity commit (including burst capacity) with pricing delta comparing fp16 vs int8 options.
3) Run a short QA on model outputs (we'll hook your eval set into Redwood Optimize to watch for regressions).

Attachments: aegisbio_kv_quant_workbook.xlsx (model memory curves by context / quant profile), aegisbio_proposal_draft.pdf (pricing outline).

Let me know if the sheet format is right and I can push more scenarios.

- Dylan
